Just wondering. By that, I mean an epiphany regarding the type of person you want to be, or changing who you are because you realise you don't like that person, that type of thing.

Looking back, I can't remember anything specific..maybe it happened over time. Or maybe that's just the way of memories. I no longer remember the details of older time, just feelings and the like.
Did you ever have a "this is who I want to be" - type moment?

I didn't really feel that in a goal-setting sort of way, but rather in a "that's not what I want to be" kind of way.

There was a point in my career that I realized I didn't want more responsibility or a larger workload...I was at a good point that gave me satisfaction and didn't push me over any stress limits. In my family life, I realized at some point that I was not an over-achieving sort of mom but was rather one that wouldn't push my kids. They excelled, but in their own way and without any influence from me besides being happy for them. And now as I head towards retirement (maybe...one day...if I am I an optimistic mood), I realise what I want is to spend time in my garden, go for long walks, and maybe take a trip once in a blue moon. I don't want to climb mountains or buy a big cottage or fly around the world.

So my mini-epiphanies were that I am happiest being average, I guess.
I am still in the process of becoming who I want to be.

It is always a process. There are those moments that can define you, but even then, your habits have to catch up with your mind.

With me, it has been a process of seeing how people view me. What do I want to be seen as? If my dad saw my today, what would he say? I think him passing away has changed me. I keep trying to mold myself into an anchor, it is this slow process, hammering at my weak spots, sharpening my key strengths. Everything I do, I think "I am going to be the best at this,, and if I am not, it better not be because of a lack of effort" I don't remember feeling like this was how I used to be, I don't remember putting that extra effort into...anything. Now I try to put that extra effort into everything.

I still have so much work to do, I started this journey later than I probably should have, but its a process, if I put in work, smart work, I will be were I need to be.

A little bit of both really. I've had a few milestones/watershed moments which I will always remember and have radically shaped me, but there's always the constant slow change of time to slowly shift those ideas.

I saw who I wanted to be but unfortunately he /she / it won't be created until after 2045. When the technological singularity hits. According to Ray Kurzweil. That person would be the future me. I found out that person may exist in the future back in 2007 or so.
I feel like if you truly become who you want to be then you'll be bored, the truth is that the climb is the most important part of it, the achievements and failures that lead you to there
